loading_fact.0: The average adult reads at 200–250 WPM. With training, 400–600 WPM is comfortable.
loading_fact.1: Speed reading reduces “saccades” — the rapid eye jumps between words that slow you down.
loading_fact.2: Sub-vocalization (silently saying words in your head) caps you around 300 WPM. Beating it is the next jump.
loading_fact.3: Comprehension typically drops above 600 WPM. Find your sweet spot.
loading_fact.4: The Guinness record for reading is over 1,000 WPM with full comprehension.
loading_fact.5: Only about 4% of your reading time is spent absorbing meaning — the rest is eye movement.
loading_fact.6: Your eye fixates on a word for ~250ms. Speed reading shortens this window.
loading_fact.7: Reading in larger chunks (4–7 words at once) can double your speed without losing meaning.
loading_fact.8: A page of dense prose averages ~250 words. Knowing this helps you pace yourself.
loading_fact.9: Skimming and speed reading are different — speed reading aims for full comprehension.
loading_fact.10: The Optimal Recognition Point (ORP) sits at ~33% of each word, where your eye naturally rests.
loading_fact.11: Most people regress 5–15% of the time, re-reading what they already read. Speed modes prevent this.
loading_fact.12: Reading on screen is ~25% slower than reading on paper, on average — focus modes close the gap.
loading_fact.13: Focus highlights the first 40% of each word — your brain fills in the rest from context.
loading_fact.14: Bolded prefixes act as visual anchors, helping your eye land precisely on each word.
loading_fact.15: The first letters of a word carry more information than the last. Focus mode leans into this.
loading_fact.16: Tap a [Tap to view…] placeholder in Focus to see the original image, table, or equation.
loading_fact.17: Scroll mode is a teleprompter — text flows past while your eyes stay still.
loading_fact.18: The yellow centre line is your fixation point. Let words come to you.
loading_fact.19: Adjust speed independently of WPM in Scroll mode — handy for skimming.
loading_fact.20: Scroll uses GPU-accelerated transforms, so it stays smooth even on long documents.

limitations.1.title: Scanned PDFs
limitations.1.body: Free version reads only digital text. Scanned or image-only PDFs require the OCR Vision add-on.
limitations.2.title: DRM-protected files
limitations.2.body: Kindle (.azw), Adobe Digital Editions (.acsm), and other DRM-locked files cannot be read.
limitations.3.title: Multi-column documents
limitations.3.body: Two-column academic papers (IEEE, ACM) may have reading-order issues in speed modes.
limitations.4.title: Tables and images
limitations.4.body: Not read word-by-word. Shown as [Object — Tap to View] placeholders. Switch to Normal View to see them.
limitations.5.title: Math equations
limitations.5.body: Skipped or shown as [Equation — Tap to View] placeholders.
limitations.6.title: Handwriting
limitations.6.body: This app is designed for printed text. Cursive or handwritten notes may not be accurately recognised even with OCR.
limitations.7.title: OCR accuracy (Image / Scan)
limitations.7.body: On-device OCR works best on flat, well-lit printed text photographed straight-on. Accuracy drops with poor lighting, angle, or low resolution.
limitations.8.title: Password-protected PDFs
limitations.8.body: Detected at import. A clear error message is shown.
limitations.9.title: RTL languages
limitations.9.body: Currently optimised for left-to-right languages only. Arabic, Hebrew, and Urdu are not supported in v1.
limitations.10.title: Offline dictionary coverage
limitations.10.body: The offline dictionary contains ~150k common words. Specialist terms may not be found.
limitations.11.title: URL reader (Pro)
limitations.11.body: Requires internet for the initial article fetch. The text is then saved offline.

nudge.disclosure.title: What FlowRead can and can't see
nudge.disclosure.body: To offer you a page before you open a distracting app, FlowRead needs Android to tell it when that app comes to the front. Here's exactly what that means.
nudge.disclosure.point1: FlowRead sees only the name of the apps you picked — nothing about any other app.
nudge.disclosure.point2: It cannot read anything on your screen. Not messages, not passwords, not what you browse.
nudge.disclosure.point3: Nothing about this leaves your device.
nudge.disclosure.off: You can turn it off in Settings, or in Android's Accessibility settings, at any time.

onboarding.perm.granted: All set. FlowRead will offer you a few pages the next time you open it.
onboarding.ready.title: Start with a book
onboarding.ready.body: A small free library, ready to read offline. Pick anything — you can import your own PDFs any time.
tip.import: That PDF rotting in your downloads folder? It could be a book by tonight.
tip.freebooks: 150 free books are already sitting in here, waiting patiently — English and Hindi.
tip.dictionary: Stuck on a word? Long-press it. Works offline, and nobody has to know.
tip.bridge: Reading a PDF? The real page is one tap away — and so is the way back. No breadcrumbs needed.
tip.engines: Five ways to read the same book. If one word at a time feels lonely, try Chunk.
tip.chapters: Long book? The chapter list is right there while you read. You needn't walk the whole way.
tip.calm: Calm mode hides everything but the words — including the things you were about to tap.
tip.offline: No internet needed, and your books never leave this phone. We couldn't read them if we tried.
tip.paste: Copied something far too long for a chat? Paste Text turns it into a book.
tip.url: Reading something in your browser? Share it to FlowRead — it's in the share sheet, where nobody ever looks.
tip.share: What you've read makes a rather good-looking card. Drawn on this phone, not on a server.
tip.nudge_settings: The apps, the timing, the daily limit — all yours. FlowRead nudges; it doesn't nag.
tip.scan: A scanned page, or a photo of one? Scan lifts the text straight out, on this phone.
settings.unlock.btn: Unlock the full power of FlowRead
dashboard.locked.title: The rest of the dashboard
dashboard.locked.item1: How your reading speed has moved, week by week
dashboard.locked.item2: Ninety days of reading, one square a day
dashboard.locked.item3: What you've finished, by file type
dashboard.locked.item4: Time left in every book you're part-way through
settings.debug.force_free.note: Pretends nothing has been purchased, so free-tier screens can be checked on this device. It can only hide features, never unlock them, and this section does not exist in a release build.
settings.debug.reset_shares.note: Forgets which books and streaks were already celebrated, so a completion prompt can be seen again. Then finish a book — the next home screen is skipped on purpose so the reader's own prompt is the one you get.
words.title: Your words
words.empty.title: No words yet
words.empty.body: Look a word up while you read and it is kept here, grouped by the book you met it in.
tip.words: Every word you look up is quietly kept. Your collection is on the home screen, getting bigger.
tip.highlights: Found a line worth keeping? Tap the highlighter, then its first and last word. Two taps, yours for good.
highlights.title: Highlights
highlights.empty.title: No highlights yet
highlights.empty.body: While reading, tap the highlighter button in the header, then tap the first and last word of the line you want to keep.
tip.highlights_screen: Your highlights are collected book by book on the home screen — the good bits, without the other 400 pages.
